newsitem.title: JAPAN: Russia budget passage crucial for palladium talks.
newsitem.headline: Russia budget passage crucial for palladium talks.

text.p: Passage of Russia's 1997 budget this Friday would eliminate a key obstacle standing in the way of talks with Japan over this year's palladium supply contracts, a Russian trade official said.

"If the budget is approved, we'll be able to clarify quickly the quantity of platinum group metals (available for export) and the schedule of export talks," said the official, who asked not to be identified.
He gave no indication when the talks could begin, although he said export licenses could be issued within a week of the budget's passage.
The official also said that Russia would have sufficient palladium stocks to meet its export contracts with Japan.

Japan-Russia talks on one-year supply contracts for palladium and other platinum group metals, usually held in mid-December, were postponed indefinitely last month due in part to a delay in the Russian budget.

Last Friday Itar-Tass news agency quoted the head of Russia's parliament, Gennady Seleznyov, as saying that Russia's 1997 draft budget was almost ready for its final reading, which is due on January 24.
